clue.text: I smear resident of Haiti, perhaps

blocks.note: taken as written
to smear someone is to slander them

explanation.surface: A confession of spreading lies about someone from Haiti.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti occupies part of the island of Hispaniola, so anyone living there is an example of an island dweller; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Death of one who bellyaches about wild mare

indicators.note: a wild animal is unruly, so the letters of the word it describes run out of order
about means going around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: to bellyache is to gripe, so a habitual complainer is a griper
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A chronic complainer comes to grief around an untamed horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Death' opens the clue as if a death is being reported; it is the definition, personified.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grim Reaper, the hooded skeleton with a scythe, is the traditional personification of death.

clue.text: Acclaim a hard downfall

blocks.note: first meaning: to praise or salute enthusiastically
second meaning: frozen pellets of ice falling from the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' suggests ruin after praise; read literally, it is something hard falling down from the clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for greeting or praising someone and a noun for ice pellets falling as precipitation.

clue.text: Actress to undress, speaking in a stereotypical French accent

indicators.text: speaking in a stereotypical French accent
indicators.note: the word is to be pronounced as a caricatured Frenchman would say it, with the short vowel lengthened

blocks.note: to undress is to strip, and a stage Frenchman stretches its short i into an ee sound

explanation.surface: An actress is told to disrobe by someone with a comic French accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Meryl Streep is the much-awarded American film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is one of the best-known film actresses, so her surname stands for an actress here.

clue.text: Militant whose favorite part of a Shakespeare play is the penultimate section?

blocks.clueFragment: a Shakespeare play is the penultimate section
blocks.note: Shakespeare's plays have five acts, so the penultimate section is Act IV
someone whose favourite part is a thing is jokingly an -ist of it, like a devotee

explanation.surface: A militant is asked which bit of a Shakespeare play they like best.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the word as ACT IV + -IST: a fan of Act IV, the penultimate of a Shakespeare play's five acts.
explanation.definitionFit: An activist campaigns vigorously for a political cause, which is what a militant does.

clue.text: Live over a field

blocks.note: to live is to be, and are is a form of be
taken as written

explanation.surface: Living above a stretch of open ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so ARE sits on top of A.
explanation.definitionFit: Field and area both mean a sphere of study or activity, as in a field or area of expertise.

clue.text: Secrecy concerning sexual orientation to face defeat in Connecticut

indicators.note: in places one word inside the letters of the other

blocks.note: to face defeat is to lose
CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut

explanation.surface: A politician in Connecticut stays secretive about their orientation and risks defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: State postal codes such as this one for Connecticut are standard in American crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the closet means concealing one's sexual orientation, so the closet stands for that secrecy.

clue.text: Reversing deficits: a crass cover for cutting

indicators.note: reversing tells you to read the run of letters from right to left
the phrase acts as a cover, the wanted word sits concealed under its letters

blocks.note: a run of letters straddling the end of deficits and the words a crass

explanation.surface: A budget hawk proposes trimming deficits, and someone accuses them of a crude cover story for spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignoring the colon and spaces, d-e-f-i-c-I-T-S-A-C-R-A-S-s read backwards gives SARCASTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is wounding and mocking, which is what a sarcastic one is; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Pink ember, initially roasting at the center

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only of the word it follows
something at the center sits in the middle of the other word, splitting it

blocks.note: a glowing ember is a piece of burning coal
the first letter of roasting

explanation.surface: A cook watches a pink-glowing ember in the middle of a roast.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into the middle of COAL: CO-R-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange colour named after the marine organism, so it serves as a shade of pink.

clue.text: Woodworker's complaint over log

blocks.note: a carp is a petty complaint, from the verb to carp
to log data is to enter it into a record

explanation.surface: A woodworker grumbles about a log that will not cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above. 'Log' looks like timber for the woodworker; it is the verb for recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a craftsman who builds and repairs wooden structures, a kind of woodworker.

clue.text: An e-mail confused a British writer

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so the preceding words are to be rearranged

blocks.note: the seven letters of these words, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: Someone reads a muddled email and is baffled by a writer from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne was the English author of Winnie-the-Pooh, so he is one example of a British writer.

clue.text: Offensive raids, no?

indicators.note: the question mark hints that the words are not to be taken at face value but scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether these raids were really offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram word: the question mark alone warns that raids and no are to be rearranged, and the two words also form part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile incursions into enemy territory, that is, raids made as part of an offensive.

clue.text: Deep sip? It is not very healthy!

definitions.text: Deep sip? It is not very healthy

indicators.note: something not very healthy is out of sorts, so the letters before it are disordered

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a long swallow of a drink and admits it is hardly good for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of Deep sip and It, being unwell, rearrange into a diet cola, and the whole clue describes that drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Diet Pepsi is a sugar-free soft drink marketed as a lighter option, yet it is still hardly a health food.

clue.text: Maniacal pastor captures red wolves

indicators.note: a maniacal version is wildly disordered, so the word it describes is rearranged
to capture is to hold within, so one set of letters encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written before being rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deranged clergyman lays traps for red wolves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red wolves' reads as a species, but red belongs to the wordplay and wolves alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolves are hunting animals that kill other animals for food, so they are predators.

clue.text: Pass a kind of sugar back before start of tea

indicators.note: going back means the sugar word is written from its end to its start
the start of a word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: cane sugar is a common kind, so cane names the kind
the first letter of tea

explanation.surface: Someone at tea declines the sugar bowl being handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like refusing the sugar at a tea table; here it is the verb for making a law.
explanation.definitionFit: When a legislature passes a bill it enacts it, turning it into law, so the verbs are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Commercial opening is the framework for traders: they believe a second coming is imminent

definitions.text: they believe a second coming is imminent

indicators.note: a framework is the outside edge of something, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
a vent is an opening
taken as written
the first and last letters of traders

explanation.surface: A business notice about a market's opening slides into talk of believers awaiting the end of days.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventists, such as Seventh-day Adventists, are Christians who expect the imminent second coming of Christ.

clue.text: Some politicians venerate priests, absurdly

indicators.note: acting absurdly is behaving without order or sense, so the words before it are jumbled

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A jab at certain lawmakers who show exaggerated reverence for the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the US House are called Representatives, so they are a particular group among elected politicians.

clue.text: Hate price of suit?

blocks.note: a suit is slang for a business executive, shortened to exec
a rate is a price charged, as for an hour of someone's time

explanation.surface: Someone loathes what a lawsuit or a new suit costs them.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as EXEC RATE, an executive's fee; a suit is slang for a corporate executive.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to detest or curse something, so it is a strong synonym of hate as a verb.

clue.text: Woman with police department nabs her clergyman

indicators.note: to nab is to grab and hold, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
PD is the standard US abbreviation for police department
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman joins the police force and arrests her own vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her clergyman' seems to be one phrase, but her is a piece of wordplay held inside the police abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd is a pastor, a minister who tends his congregation as his flock.

clue.text: Inside, Yevtushenko read The Nation at one time

indicators.note: inside says the wanted letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the poet's surname and the start of read

explanation.surface: Behind the Iron Curtain, the Soviet poet Yevtushenko once read this magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Nation' looks like this magazine's name; it means a country. Korea was a single nation until it was divided in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Korea was one unified country before its division into North and South, so it was a nation at one time.

clue.text: Collection of items to trap returning pet

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the trap word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a kit is a set of articles for a purpose
a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: Someone gathers gear to catch an animal that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' at the end seems to be the thing trapped; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a young cat, a typical household pet, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Heretical creed: a nun's stamina

indicators.note: a heretical version departs from the orthodox order, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nun holding an unorthodox creed needs staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to keep going through a long effort, which is what stamina means.

clue.text: Lisa and Ed turned clockwise

indicators.note: turned means twisted around and remixed, so the names' letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people, Lisa and Ed, rotate in the direction of a clock's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned clockwise' reads as one phrase; 'turned' is the anagram signal and 'clockwise' the definition. Deasil is an old Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deasil is a rare word for sunwise, the direction the sun travels, which is the same as clockwise.

clue.text: Switch access for oven

blocks.note: to switch someone is to whip them, and to tan a hide is to thrash it
a door is a way of access

explanation.surface: An instruction to flip the switch that opens or lights the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' reads as an on-off control; here it is the verb meaning to beat with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandoor is the clay oven of Indian and Central Asian cooking, used for naan and tandoori dishes.

clue.text: Star's deli offering

blocks.note: first meaning: a star that suddenly flares in brightness
second meaning: a kind of cured salmon sold in delicatessens

explanation.surface: A celebrity's own sandwich on a delicatessen menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Nova is the American deli name for lightly smoked salmon, short for Nova Scotia salmon, served on bagels.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly grows bright, and nova is also smoked salmon sold at a deli counter.

clue.text: After decapitation, weaken in terrible pain

indicators.note: decapitation removes the head, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to languish is to grow weak or feeble

explanation.surface: After a beheading, a victim fades away in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: LANGUISH loses its L to leave ANGUISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering, a synonym of agony or terrible pain.

clue.text: Valley girl's, like, exciting? Not at first
The king's article in Spain, with permission to travel curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed literally means having the tail cut off, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: el is the Spanish definite article
a visa is an official permission to enter or travel in a country

explanation.surface: A monarch's newspaper article in Spain notes that his travel permit was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: VISA loses its last letter. 'The king' is not a monarch here: Elvis Presley is known as the King of Rock and Roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's popular nickname is the King, short for the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Decorate trees strangely for three months

indicators.note: arranged strangely means set out in an odd order, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: to trim a dress or a Christmas tree is to decorate it
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: Odd instructions to dress up the trees for a season.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a period of about three months, as in the three stages of a pregnancy.
